local part = workspace.Part
local connections = getconnections(part.Touched)

for i, connection in ipairs(connections) do
    print("Connection", i)
    print("  Function:", connection.Function)
    print("  State:", connection.State)
    print("  Thread:", connection.Thread)

    connection.Disable()  -- Disables this connection

    connection.Disconnect()  -- Disconnects this connection

name: checkcaller
description: Returns whether the function currently running was called by Zenith.

returns.description: true if the current function was called by Zenith, false otherwise

examples.description: Check if code is running from the executor
examples.code:
local refs = {}

refs.__namecall = hookmetamethod(game, "__namecall", function(...)
	local self = ...
	local isRunningOnExecutor = checkcaller()

	if isRunningOnExecutor then
		-- The executor invoked the __namecall method, so this will not affect the
		-- scripts in the game.
		if self == game then
			error("No __namecall on game allowed")
		end
	end

	return refs.__namecall(...)
end)

game:Destroy() --> Error "No __namecall on game allowed"

notes: This is useful for metamethod hooks that need to behave differently when called by the game versus when called by Zenith.

name: hookmetamethod
description: Redirects calls to a metamethod with a custom hook function and returns the original metamethod.
syntax: hookmetamethod(object: table, method: string, hook: function): function

params.name: object
params.description: The table whose metamethod will be hooked

params.name: method
params.description: The name of the metamethod to hook (e.g., "__index", "__namecall")

params.name: hook
params.description: The function that will replace the original metamethod

returns.description: The original metamethod that was replaced

examples.code:
local old = hookmetamethod(game, "__namecall", function(...)
	local method = getnamecallmethod()
	local self = ...
	
	if method == "HttpGet" then
		print("HttpGet called on:", self)
	end
	
	return old(...)
end)

notes: Always store and call the original metamethod to maintain proper functionality. Use checkcaller() within hooks to differentiate between executor and game calls.

name: getcallingscript
description: Returns the script responsible for the currently running function.

returns.description: The script that called the current function

examples.description: Get the script that called a function
examples.code:
local refs = {}
local bannedScripts = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer.PlayerGui

refs.__namecall = hookmetamethod(game, "__namecall", function(...)
	local caller = getcallingscript()

	-- Use '.' notation to call the IsDescendantOf method without invoking
	-- __namecall and causing a recursive loop.
	local isBanned = caller.IsDescendantOf(caller, bannedScripts)

	if isBanned then
		error("Not allowed to invoke __namecall")
	end

	return refs.__namecall(...)
end)

name: restorefunction
description: Restores a hooked function to its prior state.

notes: This function will error if the function has not been hooked.
